packs.title: Capital, River and Neighborhoods
packs.promise: Explore Sacramento through civic places, local history, gardens and river paths.

q.s: Compare a historic wing with a newer one.
st: Find one visible feature of the historic building and one of the newer museum wing.
Describe their materials or shapes without judging either as better.
Make a two-column sketch or note about how each invites a visitor in.

q.s: Build a color key without expecting a bloom.
st: From an open garden path, choose three colors or textures visible today.
Arrange them into a small key for this season; note whether flowers, leaves or paths provided the strongest color.

q.s: Build a small public-park comfort map.
st: Find an open path, shade and a place to sit without entering ticketed attractions.
Describe how far each is from your chosen safe starting point using near/far rather than a measured distance.
Choose a comfortable route between the three, including a way to shorten it.

packs.title: Old Waterfront on Foot
packs.promise: Find ten small stories within the connected Old Sacramento waterfront.

st: Observe two ground-floor features from the public path.
Read the State Parks account of merchant rooms and railroad offices.
Make a two-column note: one visible feature and one historical use; do not assume the current interior is open.

q.s: Turn one statue into a route note.
st: Study the outdoor monument without climbing it.
Name one sculpted motion cue and one way the sender would have waited for news.
Write a two-line message from an invented traveler; label it as fiction, not a historical quotation.
Choose an open viewpoint away from traffic and the river edge.
Find one bridge line that connects the banks and one line that rises above the roadway.
Describe how those two lines guide your eye toward the far side.
